Chapter 9: How Marriage Shapes and Sanctifies
You know, marriage really has a way of showing us who we are—sometimes in ways we never expected.
There’s this closeness, the daily routines, all those shared responsibilities... and suddenly, the best and worst parts of ourselves start to surface.
It’s almost like marriage holds up a mirror—not just reflecting the polished version we want to see, but also the sides of ourselves we might rather keep hidden.
Have you ever found yourself in a familiar argument, and out of nowhere, you catch a glimpse of your own stubbornness?
It can be so uncomfortable—maybe even a little painful.
But right there, something important happens. You start to realize that marriage isn’t just about hoping your partner will change. It’s about letting yourself be changed too.
Most of us step into marriage expecting happiness. But pretty quickly, we see that happiness isn’t always the main goal.
Marriage is really more like a workshop for the soul—a place where we grow.
Think about the daily challenges: learning to really listen, to compromise, to forgive.
These aren’t just hurdles—they’re chances to transform.
And over time, something incredible happens. Those rough edges? They start to smooth out.
Patience grows. Empathy gets deeper. And your ability to love? It expands in ways you wouldn’t expect.
The truth is, most of us don’t notice these changes as they’re happening. But when you look back, it hits you—marriage has shaped you into someone more generous, more resilient, more whole than before.
If you’re willing to be open, marriage can really become a path of sanctification—a way to become more fully yourself, and even more capable of loving others.
It’s never about being perfect. It’s about making progress together.
And maybe the real miracle isn’t that two people fit together perfectly, but that, together, they help each other become so much more than they could’ve been alone.
